identity_policy: name is the sound-request name (NAME/REQD); wave is the verified WAVE index. ghidra rows carry reqd+tone and must satisfy TONE[tone].wave == wave. audition rows carry verified_index=true and are explicitly not chain-proven.

cues.name: boss01_vo_atk1
cues.chain: NAME hash(boss01_vo_atk1) -> REQD 340 -> SEQD 0x10B1 -> request-order tone 20 -> TONE[20] = (key 34, wave 3); TONE[18..24] -> waves 1..7 and the request order after ground1 is ground2, ground3, vo_atk1, vo_atk2, vo_atk3, vo_dmg1, vo_dmg2
cues.note: The tone->wave step is binary (flat boss01 TONE table); the name->tone step is the request/play-list order, hence medium confidence. The 0x42 pair 108/109 is a large roar alternative, not this row.

cues.name: boss01_atk_hit_ground1
cues.chain: NAME hash(boss01_atk_hit_ground1) -> REQD 303 -> SEQD timeline 0x13E4 -> bytecode 0x23BA -> a4 01 43 -> TONE[43] = (key 57, wave 26); the sequence then plays tones 44-47 -> waves 27-30
cues.note: Layered sound: the request is the 5-layer ground impact; wave 26 is the first and longest layer. wave_pool_label is the pool string at index 26, which is not the request name.

cues.note: The tone->wave step is binary; the name->tone step is the request/play-list order, hence medium confidence.
